title: are Sikhs Hindu or Muslim?
hookLine: the question Sikhs get asked from both sides, and the plain answer: a learner, on a path of its own
carry: a learner, on a path of its own

cards: So, are Sikhs a kind of Hindu? Or a kind of Muslim? Sikhs hear both, sometimes in the same week.

Surveys in the United States have found many people guessing Sikhism is a branch of Islam; others assume it's part of Hinduism. The plain answer is neither. And why people mix it up turns out to be a good story.

teach.b: Start with the word. Sikh is Punjabi for a learner, a student: someone who learns from the Guru. So nobody starts out finished.

teach.h: ITS OWN PATH, FROM GURU NANAK.
teach.b: The path began with Guru Nanak, born, tradition says, in 1469, in Punjab, and grew through ten Gurus over about two hundred years.
It has its own scripture, its own initiation, which you met on day four, and its own houses of worship. So it's a religion of its own, not a branch of another. Why the mix-up?
Nanak was born into a Hindu family and grew up among Hindu and Muslim neighbors. His companion on years of travel, Mardana, was a Muslim musician.
Sikh scripture uses names for God that both neighbors used, and it even holds hymns by holy poets born into Hindu and Muslim families, beside the Gurus' own.

teach.h: SHARING WORDS ISN'T BEING THE SAME.
teach.b: Sharing words isn't the same as being the same. Then there's the turban and the beard, which people who don't know often read as Muslim, and that mistake hasn't always been harmless.

teach.h: THERE IS NO HINDU, THERE IS NO MUSLIM.
teach.b: The first words Nanak is remembered saying, as his mission began, were: there is no Hindu, there is no Muslim. Some hear in that: beneath the labels, everyone is made by the one.
Others hear a challenge: nobody was living up to the name they carried. Either way, it put no one down. It was a starting point.

how: Sikhs follow the teaching of the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib, with their own initiation and gurdwaras; many explain Sikhi to friends simply as its own religion, begun by Guru Nanak in Punjab about five hundred years ago.

games.q: who's who, and what's what — tap the pairs.

it's a religion of its own, begun by Guru Nanak in Punjab about five hundred years ago.
Sikh scripture holds hymns by poets born into Hindu and Muslim families
devotees like Namdev and the Sufi Sheikh Farid sit beside the Gurus.

games.q: a coworker asks, kindly: so Sikhs are a kind of Muslim, right? what's the plain answer?
o: no: Sikhi is its own path, begun by Guru Nanak in Punjab.
games.why: plain and kind: a religion of its own, about five hundred years old, from Punjab.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, notice one label people put on you. On the second, notice one you put on someone else.
On the third, set both down for a breath, and see the person underneath.

wordCard.voice: Sikh. A learner, a student of the Guru, on a path that began with Guru Nanak. Sixth word.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: a learner, a disciple; from the Sanskrit shishya, a student.

carryVoice: Your line: a learner, on a path of its own. That's the plain answer, and it needs nobody else's faith put down to say it. See you tomorrow.
